page: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64g-480s is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provided via a bundled 480 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities alongside balanced multi-core throughput. The server achieves top-tier status in single-core stress-ng CPU tests and single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests, falls within the average tier. Memory bandwidth is stable, registering 881.03 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and approximately 71.86 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For specialized workloads, the AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions.

This hardware profile offers a cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. While the server excels at single-threaded execution and small-model LLM text generation, it exhibits weaker performance in prompt processing for larger models, such as the 7B parameter LLM. Consequently, this instance is well-suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
